# MatrixCore — Set up the quality gate in your project

Project-agnostic engine setup. Works with the plain CLI, CI, or any supported MCP host. Native host
integration lives under `integrations/`; Cline setup is documented in `INSTALL_CLINE.md`.

## 1. Pre-reqs

- Node.js, npm, and git.
- The toolchain the checks need. Verify with the engine's doctor:

  ```bash
  npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.0
  npx --no-install matrix-core doctor
  ```

  Required workspace binaries must match the embedded exact policy: Ruff 0.16.1, mypy 2.3.0,
  Xenon 0.9.3, and deptry 0.25.1 for Python; SQLFluff 4.2.2 for declared SQL facets; TypeScript
  5.9.3 and ESLint 9.39.5 for TypeScript.

## 2. Git repo (required for a stable gate version)

The gate certifies a workspace version = git HEAD + sorted (path, state, content-hash) of every
changed/untracked file. `git init` if not a repo — otherwise the engine hashes the entire tree (including
`.venv`, caches), which is slow and changes on every run, so the gate would block every completion as stale.

```bash
git init
```

## 3. Ignore churn

Any file a check writes or that changes while you work must be ignored, or it flips the workspace version
mid-work and invalidates the last PASS. Add to `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
.quality/
coverage.json
coverage.xml
.coverage
node_modules/
dist/
.venv/
venv/
__pycache__/
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.pytest_cache/
*.db
*.db-shm
*.db-wal
.env
```

Add project-specific artifacts too (generated exports, keychain dumps, etc.). Verify nothing churns:

```bash
git status --porcelain   # only stable source files
```

## 4. quality.yaml

```yaml
version: 2
project: my-application
review:
  agentsmith: true
```

The embedded policy approves role-specific 9B and 122B profiles. Bind review roles by
profile ID when selecting models:

```yaml
review:
  agentsmith: true
  mode: auto
  models:
    candidate: qwen35-9b-local
    scout: qwen35-122b-scout-local
    verifier: qwen35-9b-verifier-local
```

Install only the models you intend to use; MatrixCore never downloads them implicitly:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M
ollama pull qwen3.5:122b-a10b
```

For SQLite SQL embedded in Python, add only application-resolution metadata:

```yaml
application:
  sql:
    - root: finance
      dialect: sqlite
      templater: raw
      sources: [files, python]
```

## 5. Run

```bash
# from the configured project
npx --no-install matrix-core run --changed --fast
npx --no-install matrix-core completion
```

### Nested projects

MatrixCore discovers nested package roots from application manifests and lockfiles. Use
`matrix-core workspace show` to inspect ownership and `matrix-core policy show` to inspect the
centrally owned checks, versions, assets, and hashes.

## 6. Reading the output

- Per-check status is PASS / FAIL / ERROR. Missing or incompatible required tools fail closed.
- The terminal gate is **immutable and versioned**: `completion-gate.json` is replaced only by a
  terminal `PASS`/`FAIL`. Active-run and lock artifacts are separate, so a duplicate start cannot
  erase a current PASS.

## 7. Caveats

- `quality run` and MCP `quality_run` use the same gate service and persist identical evidence.
- Concurrent CLI/MCP completion requests are serialized per repository and reuse one result.
- `--changed` needs a git repo; consumer gates never invoke application tests.
- `completion` runs the central deterministic profile and runs the central AgentSmith profile only
  when `review.agentsmith: true` is declared in the v2 manifest.
- AgentSmith results are advisory and remain reported even when partial or unavailable; exact-state
  deterministic PASS controls completion authorization.
- Completion enforcement uses each host's native hook and the shared `matrixcore-hook` executable.
- Planning-only turns bypass completion enforcement before workspace resolution.

## 8. Agent enforcement

Install the appropriate native integration from `integrations/`. For Cline, see `INSTALL_CLINE.md`.
fileContents.POLICY_BUNDLES.md:
# GitHub policy bundles

MatrixCore can consume a declarative policy bundle from a public GitHub repository without a policy server.
GitHub is used only by an explicit synchronization command. Gates, reviews, status checks, MCP tools, and hooks
read a verified local cache and never access the network.

## Project configuration

```yaml
version: 2
project: example
policy:
  source: github
  repository: acme/quality-policy
  ref: stable
  manifest: matrixcore/policy.json
review:
  agentsmith: true
  mode: auto
  models:
    candidate: qwen35-9b-local
    scout: qwen35-122b-scout-local
    verifier: qwen35-9b-verifier-local
```

The repository and ref are project-owned. `ref` may be a branch, tag, or commit. MatrixCore resolves it to an
immutable commit only during synchronization.

```bash
# Deliberately advance the configured ref and update the committed lock.
quality policy sync

# Restore exactly what the committed lock names; used by CI and new workstations.
quality policy sync --locked

# These commands never use the network.
quality policy status
quality policy show
quality run --full
```

Commit `matrixcore-policy.lock.json`. Keep `.quality/` ignored; verified bundles are cached under
`.quality/policies/<policyHash>/`. A remote-policy project with no valid lock/cache fails closed and tells the user
which sync command to run. It never falls back to a different embedded policy.

## Contract

The machine contract is `dist/policy/github-policy-bundle.schema.json`. A v1 `policy.json` declares:

- a policy ID and minimum MatrixCore version;
- installed MatrixCore check IDs, exact tool versions, and check-specific typed settings;
- locked AgentSmith model profiles, default role bindings, routing, graph, partitioning, evidence, and verification policy;
- data and Markdown assets with byte sizes, media types, and SHA-256 digests.

Policy bundles cannot define raw commands, plugins, JavaScript, shell files, or executable scripts. Unknown checks
fail with an instruction to update MatrixCore. Executable adapters and helpers remain part of the audited npm
package. The v1 TypeScript ESLint policy uses the `embedded-recommended` executable profile while the remote
manifest controls its exact tool version and zero-warning setting.

Supported typed settings are:

| Check | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| `python.ruff`, `python.ruff-format`, `python.mypy`, `typescript.tsc`, `sql.sqlfluff` | `configAsset` |
| `python.xenon` | `configAsset`, `maxAbsolute`, `maxModules`, `maxAverage`, `ignore`, `exclude` |
| `python.deptry` | `ignore` containing `DEPnnn` codes |
| `typescript.eslint` | `profile: embedded-recommended`, `maxWarnings: 0` |

AgentSmith uses the fixed `agentsmith/` layout for review assets, including the structured
`rules/registry.yaml`. Every referenced file must appear in the manifest asset inventory. Projects may bind
candidate, scout, and verifier roles only to model profile IDs declared by the locked policy.

## Identity and trust

The lock records the configured source, resolved 40-character commit, raw manifest digest, content-derived policy
hash, every asset digest, and a reviewable check/profile summary. The policy hash is SHA-256 over canonical JSON
plus the lexically sorted `path:sha256` asset inventory. Gate and review evidence includes that hash.

V1 trusts GitHub TLS and the public repository selected by the project. It does not support tokens, private
repositories, signatures, downloaded code, automatic updates, or background network traffic. Review sync diffs
and the lock-file change before committing them.
fileContents.README.md:
# MatrixCore - Language Agnostic

Core-first quality engine with a universal local MCP tool interface and native host
completion hooks. The engine owns validation, review, artifacts, and policy.

```
matrix-core
├── core/
│   ├── runner, gate (terminal PASS/FAIL plus separate active-run state), version, gate-store, reviewer, cli
├── agentsmith/
│   ├── agents/ (orchestrator + sub-agents + security), rules/, scripts/ pipeline, skills/
├── packs/
│   ├── python/ centrally configured ruff, ruff-format, mypy, xenon, deptry
│   ├── sql/ centrally configured sqlfluff plus embedded-Python extraction
│   └── typescript/ centrally configured tsc, eslint
├── policy/ (embedded defaults plus the GitHub bundle contract schema)
├── mcp/ (quality_run, quality_status, quality_fix over local stdio)
├── hooks/ (shared completion policy + host response envelopes)
└── integrations/ (Codex, Claude Code, and Cline native configuration)
```

**Status matrix:** PluginResult `PASS|FAIL|SKIPPED|ERROR`
- SKIPPED = env limitation not code defect
- FAIL = code violates or required binary missing
- ERROR = engine malfunction
- PASS = ok

**Gate model:** deterministic runs record schema-v2 evidence containing execution mode,
fast/full semantics, base branch, and changed-file scope. Changed feedback is stored in
`.quality/changed-gate.json`; full evidence is stored in `.quality/completion-gate.json`.
Native completion hooks never run the engine and accept only a current, non-fast full PASS.
Starting another completion run does not overwrite terminal evidence with `RUNNING`; completion
calls are serialized per repository and active-run state is stored separately.

## Build
```bash
npm install
npm run build
node dist/core/cli.js doctor
node dist/core/cli.js run
```

Public project installation uses the published package:

```bash
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.1
npx --no-install matrix-core doctor
```

Read [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the shared holistic, partitioned, and hybrid review
pipeline.

## Config resolution (monorepo)
flag `--config` > CWD `quality.yaml` > parents upward > `.git` root > default embedded, nearest wins.

## quality.yaml template

```yaml
version: 2
project: my-application
review:
  agentsmith: true
```

Advisory review bounds are configurable. Defaults are conservative for slow local models: one
in-flight model call (`parallelism: 1`), four partitioned candidate work items, four verifier
candidates, and a total review deadline of `180000ms`. Faster providers can raise caps:

```yaml
review:
  agentsmith: true
  parallelism: 4
  maxDurationMs: 600000
```

Timeout and token-budget results are explicit partial reviews, never approval. See
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [src/agentsmith/README.md](src/agentsmith/README.md).

SQLite applications with SQL embedded in Python declare application-resolution metadata without
selecting quality rules:

```yaml
application:
  sql:
    - root: finance
      dialect: sqlite
      templater: raw
      sources: [files, python]
```

The v2 manifest is intentionally strict. By default, projects may opt into AgentSmith but use MatrixCore's
immutable embedded policy. A project may instead select one complete declarative policy bundle from a public
GitHub repository; it cannot inject commands or executable policy code. See [POLICY_BUNDLES.md](POLICY_BUNDLES.md).
V1 manifests are rejected with migration guidance.

## CLI
```bash
quality doctor
quality run --full
quality run --changed --base main
quality run --json
quality status --json
quality review --json
quality workspace show --json
quality policy show --json
quality policy status --json
quality policy sync
quality policy sync --locked
quality fix --review-version <version> --finding <id...>
quality trace status
quality eval list
quality config show
```

## Local AgentSmith traces and evals

AgentSmith tracing is a local diagnostic feature, not telemetry. It captures locally by default,
retaining the newest 20 traces within a 250 MiB budget. MatrixCore contains no trace uploader or
analytics endpoint. Disable capture explicitly with `MATRIXCORE_TRACE=off`; use
`MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith` to label a run as explicitly captured:

```bash
MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith quality completion
quality trace status
quality trace list
quality trace show <trace-id>
quality trace metrics <trace-id>
```

Enabled traces are private local files under `.quality/traces/agentsmith/`. They contain the frozen
snapshot, route decision, projection audits, work items, exact prompts and raw provider responses,
evidence resolution, verification, coverage, and decision provenance. `quality doctor`
warns when tracing is enabled and `.quality/` is not ignored by Git. Trace write failures never change
the review or completion decision.

Promote a deliberately selected trace into an editable regression case, label expected bugs L0-L3,
then compare candidate-generation strategies against the same frozen snapshot:

```bash
quality eval curate --trace <trace-id> --case <slug>
quality eval run --case <slug> --mode all --replay planner
quality eval run --case <slug> --mode all --replay recorded
quality eval run --case <slug> --mode all --replay live
quality eval compare <baseline-result.json> <current-result.json>
```

Curated cases are written to `evals/agentsmith/<slug>/`. Inspect `input.json` and `case.yaml` for
proprietary code, credentials, prompts, and personal data before committing them. Eval reports remain
ignored under `.quality/evals/runs/`. No trace is ever curated, committed, or transmitted automatically.
Curated `originalCandidates` can be labeled accepted or rejected, and
`expectedInspectionTargets` can name files, symbols, and graph edges that a sound planner must inspect.
Planner replay measures deterministic selection and coverage without an LLM. Recorded replay requires
exact prompt/model matches and detects strategy drift; live replay measures the complete current stack.
Reports include finding quality only when it is evaluable, plus file/changed-line coverage, target
recall, candidate adjudication, evidence relevance, reliability, latency, token use, and explicit
honesty checks. Rejected candidates must never become verified findings; likely, rejected, and
insufficient-evidence outcomes remain trace/eval data only.

## Deterministic profiles

- Python: Ruff lint, Ruff format check, mypy, Xenon with B/B/A limits, and deptry DEP004.
- SQL: SQLFluff using MatrixCore's bundled rules. Declared Python facets extract DB-API SQL literals,
  constants, and static concatenations; unresolved executed SQL fails closed.
- TypeScript: `tsc --noEmit` with MatrixCore quality overrides and ESLint using MatrixCore's bundled flat config.

The default embedded policy requires Ruff 0.16.1, mypy 2.3.0, Xenon 0.9.3, deptry 0.25.1,
SQLFluff 4.2.2, TypeScript 5.9.3, and ESLint 9.39.5 exactly. Consumers provision applicable
binaries in their designated workspace environments.

Application tests, coverage, builds, and application-specific validation are not part of the consumer
gate. Required tools must come from the resolved workspace environment and satisfy the central version
policy; missing or incompatible tools fail closed.

## Universal agent integration

Install MatrixCore in the project so its CLI, MCP server, and hook executable are available to local package resolution:

```bash
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.0
```

All hosts receive `quality_run`, `quality_status`, and `quality_fix` from the same local
stdio MCP server. Codex and Claude Code plugins bundle native Stop hooks; Cline uses
its native TaskComplete hook. The supplied integrations invoke the local package with
`npx --no-install`, which never downloads a missing package. See `integrations/README.md`
and `INSTALL_CLINE.md`.

Planning-only host turns bypass completion enforcement before workspace resolution. Default/code
mode remains fail-closed.

`quality_run(mode=completion)` runs MatrixCore's deterministic profile, then runs MatrixCore's
AgentSmith profile only when the project opts in. Application test policy remains independent.
`quality_fix` hands a version-bound repair task to the active Cline, Codex, or Claude Code
model. Ollama reviews code but never authors fixes.

### Select a review model

The embedded policy approves role-specific local profiles. Projects select role bindings by profile ID;
arbitrary model names are rejected:

```yaml
review:
  agentsmith: true
  mode: auto
  models:
    candidate: qwen35-9b-local
    scout: qwen35-122b-scout-local
    verifier: qwen35-9b-verifier-local
```

This is the recommended hybrid configuration. Use `qwen35-122b-local` as `candidate` for
holistic-first review when the complete projection fits. Install selected models explicitly:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M
ollama pull qwen3.5:122b-a10b
```

MatrixCore does not download models during installation or review.

Project setup (git init, .gitignore, quality.yaml, engine verify) is project-agnostic — see
`INSTALL_PROJECT.md`.

During plugin development, run `npm run plugin:sync` after changing the Codex manifest, skill,
hook, or MCP configuration. The command derives the plugin base version from `package.json` and
records a new immutable cachebuster. `npm pack` runs `plugin:check` and fails if the versions or
plugin fingerprint have diverged.

## Doctor example
```
[core] node ✓, git ✓
[python:.] python ✓, ruff ✓, mypy ✓, xenon ✓, deptry ✓
[sql:finance] python ✓, sqlfluff ✓
[typescript:frontend] node ✓, tsc ✓, eslint ✓
Doctor: PASSED
```

## Ignore
```
.quality/
coverage.json
coverage.xml
.coverage
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.pytest_cache/
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.env
.DS_Store
dist/
node_modules/
```

# Incorporate into projects

## 1. Add to new Python repo

```bash
cd my-py-service
npm init -y
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.0
cat > quality.yaml <<'Y'
version: 2
project: my-py-service
review:
  agentsmith: false
Y
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install ruff==0.16.1 mypy==2.3.0 xenon==0.9.3 deptry==0.25.1
npx quality doctor
npx quality run
```

## 2. Agent host integration

Install the MatrixCore package, then enable the Codex, Claude Code, or Cline bundle described in
`integrations/README.md`. Every host receives the same MCP tools and native completion policy.

## 3. Ensure git status clean after init

```bash
echo ".quality/\ncoverage.json\ndist/\nnode_modules/" >> .gitignore
git add quality.yaml package.json USAGE.md
```

## 4. Commands reference

- `quality doctor` → capability matrix PASS/FAIL (required missing = fail)
- `quality run` → full
- `quality run --fast` → central format/lint/type checks on the current scope
- `quality run --changed --fast` → fast stage on git diff vs main (in-turn LLM loop)
- `quality run --changed` → all enabled checks on git diff vs main
- `quality run --file <path>` → single file, implies changed mode
- `quality run --json` → machine output for tool

## 5. Central policy

The default embedded profile cannot be altered by projects. `matrix-core workspace show` explains
package ownership and environments; `matrix-core policy show` prints effective checks, required
versions, bundled configuration assets, and hashes. Missing or incompatible designated tools fail.

Projects may opt into a complete declarative policy from a public GitHub repository. Updates are explicit:
`quality policy sync` advances the configured ref and writes `matrixcore-policy.lock.json`, while
`quality policy sync --locked` restores that exact commit. Normal validation never uses the network and fails
closed when the locked cache is unavailable. See `POLICY_BUNDLES.md`.

## 6. Link workflow

Engine already lints itself (this repo). Example success run:

```
Node ✓, git ✓, python ✓, ruff ✓, mypy ✓, xenon ✓, deptry ✓, tsc ✓, eslint ✓
Doctor PASSED
Run PASS with workspace and policy hashes
```

## 7. Published package

The current public release is `0.5.0`:

```bash
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.0
```

## 8. Versioned gate + universal completion enforcement

The expensive operation runs through the `quality_run` **tool** (60s tool budget), not a hook.
Hooks only enforce state.

```
agent turn
  |
quality_run(mode=completion) [tool, configured completion workflow]
  |
  +-- deterministic checks
  +-- GateResult{version, mode=full, fast=false, status, checks} -> .quality/completion-gate.json
  +-- active coordination -> .quality/completion-run.json + completion.lock
  +-- gate.log + host logger
  |
host attempts completion
  |
native Stop/TaskComplete hook [recompute repository/policy identity + read persisted evidence]
  |
  full/non-fast gate exists? version == current? status == PASS?
    |-- no/FAILED/EXPIRED/stale -> { skip, reason }
    +-- all ok -> completion allowed
```

- `matrixcore-hook` translates Cline TaskComplete and Codex/Claude Stop payloads into one shared
  completion decision. It recomputes the workspace version and reads `.quality/completion-gate.json`;
  it never runs the engine.
- Changed/fast feedback is stored independently in `.quality/changed-gate.json` and can never
  authorize completion or overwrite the last full result.
- Terminal gate evidence is **immutable and versioned**. `completion-gate.json` contains the last
  terminal `PASS` or `FAIL`; active state and the cross-process lease are separate. Concurrent MCP
  and CLI callers join one completion run instead of replacing terminal evidence or running twice.
  Completion is blocked when terminal evidence is missing, failed, expired, or stale.
- Every gate outcome is written to `<workspaceRoot>/.quality/gate.log`. Watch live with
  `tail -f .quality/gate.log`. Example lines:

  ```
  2026-08-04T21:33:29.535Z [INFO] quality_run(mode=full) PASS in 2616ms (version f3f37c8d5ae5)
  2026-08-04T21:33:36.058Z [WARN] completion blocked - workspace changed since gate
  ```

Host hooks block until a current deterministic PASS exists. AgentSmith remains advisory: completed,
partial, timed-out, and provider-error results stay visible in the completion evidence but do not
change deterministic authorization. Findings remain user-selected for any later fix turn.

## 9. Local review traces

Trace capture is off unless the local process explicitly sets `MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith`. This is
intentionally separate from `quality.yaml`, so a repository cannot silently enable capture for its
contributors. MatrixCore writes only to `.quality/traces/agentsmith/` and has no upload capability.

```bash
MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith quality review
quality trace status
quality trace list
quality eval curate --trace <trace-id> --case <slug>
quality eval run --mode all --repeat 1
```

Edit the curated `case.yaml` to accept or reject original findings, add missed expected findings,
record narrative follow-up and true code flow, and identify required context. Exact replay measures
model variability; current replay applies the current reviewer assets to the frozen input. The eval
report includes finding precision/recall/F1, verdicts, rejected claims, errors, latency, and required
context coverage. A human-rejected original claim may disappear or remain rejected, but the eval fails
if it is promoted into the validated findings that influence the verdict. Always sanitize a case before
adding it to source control.

The full consumer profile includes Ruff, Ruff format, mypy, Xenon, and deptry for Python; tsc and
ESLint for TypeScript; and SQLFluff for explicitly declared SQL facets. MatrixCore discovers nested
package roots automatically. A manifest may select one locked GitHub policy bundle but cannot directly add raw
commands, scripts, or executable plugins.
fileContents.integrations/README.md:
# Host integrations

MatrixCore uses one local stdio MCP server and one portable completion hook. Install the published
exact version in every project with `npm install --save-dev --save-exact @epv44/matrixcore@0.5.0`;
integrations use `npx --no-install` to resolve only that project-local package without downloading
at runtime.

## Codex

Add this repository as a local marketplace, install the `matrix-core` plugin, review and trust its Stop hook, then start a new thread.

## Claude Code

Load `integrations/claude-code/matrix-core` as a plugin. It starts the same MCP server and bundles a native Stop hook.

## Cline

Merge `integrations/cline/cline_mcp_settings.fragment.json` into Cline's MCP settings. Copy the platform-appropriate `TaskComplete` hook into the global Cline hooks directory or the repository's `.clinerules/hooks/` directory and enable hooks. The extensionless file is for macOS/Linux; the PowerShell file is for Windows.

For Cline SDK, CLI, or Kanban, install `integrations/cline/plugin.ts` with Cline's plugin installer. The host supplies `@cline/sdk`; the plugin uses the same local `matrixcore-hook` binary and enforces `turn_end`. The native TaskComplete hook remains the path for editor extensions.

The hook does nothing in repositories without `quality.yaml`. In configured repositories it requires a current deterministic PASS and, when that project opts into AgentSmith, a current advisory review attempt. MatrixCore uses either its embedded policy or the project's verified, locked GitHub policy bundle; bundles remain declarative and can reference only checks implemented by the installed client. Application tests remain separate project scripts and CI jobs.

fileContents.src/agentsmith/README.md:
# AgentSmith unified review engine

The public architecture overview is [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md). This document
focuses on AgentSmith implementation and policy details.

AgentSmith freezes one immutable review snapshot and routes it through a shared repository graph, projection planner, structured rule registry, evidence resolver, verifier, deduplicator, coverage model, trace schema, and final result contract.

Candidate generation adapts to locked model profiles selected by the project:

- **holistic** — a strong model reviews the complete eligible projection when it fits with configured headroom;
- **partitioned** — a smaller model reviews semantic local units and proactive graph interaction units;
- **hybrid** — a strong compact scout prioritizes local and interaction units inspected by the candidate model.

Partitioned and hybrid candidate generation are risk-ranked and bounded by policy: the embedded
defaults select at most four candidate work items, generate at most two candidates per work item,
and verify at most four candidates, with optional
explicit candidate and verification token budgets (defaults are twice the corresponding model input
budget). Each work item includes at most four concise rules. Parallelism defaults to one in-flight
model call and the total review deadline defaults to 600000ms. Lower-ranked and token-budget-omitted changes remain in the frozen scope and are reported
as explicit coverage omissions. When the deadline fires, no new scout, candidate, or verifier calls
start, in-flight provider calls are aborted, completed candidates, evidence, and verified findings
are preserved, and unfinished work is reported as timeout omissions; the result is explicitly
partial and never presented as approval.

Context size is a packing constraint, not a product boundary. Automatic routing uses 70% of the selected profile's context at most and reserves explicit reasoning/output space. Unknown models cannot be inferred as strong from their names; they must be declared in an embedded or locked GitHub policy profile.

## Pipeline

1. Capture committed, staged, unstaged, untracked, renamed, and deleted changes, retaining deleted preimages and all omissions.
2. Build the Python/TypeScript repository graph and derive changed symbols from hunk overlap.
3. Construct complete and compact projections with deterministic token estimates and selection audits.
4. Route to holistic, partitioned, or hybrid candidate generation.
5. Normalize candidates into one v2 contract.
6. Resolve bounded structural evidence from the frozen graph and repository.
7. Verify every publishable candidate with the configured low-output verifier profile.
8. Publish only verified findings, then deduplicate, rank, and report actual file/symbol/edge/evidence coverage.

An empty partial/error result is `incomplete`, never approval. Findings must anchor to changed hunks; unchanged files can support evidence but cannot become finding locations.

## Project model roles

```yaml
review:
  agentsmith: true
  mode: auto
  models:
    candidate: qwen35-9b-local
    scout: qwen35-122b-scout-local
    verifier: qwen35-9b-verifier-local
```

Projects may select only profiles approved by the active policy. A forced mode that cannot run with those profiles fails explicitly.

Candidate generation uses a compact bounded wire schema and expands it into the stable internal finding contract. The default candidate profile allows 4096 output tokens with a 240-second request timeout; the verifier uses 512 tokens with 120 seconds. The opt-in 122B scout uses 1024 tokens with 180 seconds. Ollama model residency is kept alive for the review budget plus five minutes (15 minutes under the default policy).

`ReviewProvider` implements `health(signal)` and `invoke({ profile, prompt, outputKind, allowedFiles, maxCandidates, signal })`, returning raw output, token usage, and optional completion metadata. Providers never download models implicitly.

## Local traces and evals

Tracing is local by default and has no uploader. It retains the newest 20 schema-v2 traces within a
250 MiB budget under `.quality/traces/agentsmith/`. Set `MATRIXCORE_TRACE=off` to disable it, or
`MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith` to mark an explicitly captured run. Traces include projections, work
items, prompts, raw responses (including structured-output failures), completion metadata, evidence,
verification outcomes, coverage, and final provenance.

Curated eval cases replay the same snapshot through holistic, partitioned-local,
partitioned-evidence, partitioned-interactions, and hybrid modes. Cases label expected findings L0-L3
and may declare required file, symbol, and graph-edge inspection targets. Three replay backends isolate
different questions: `planner` evaluates deterministic selection without an LLM, `recorded` reuses
exact captured model responses and fails on prompt/model drift, and `live` runs the current provider.
Reports separate finding quality from coverage and include changed-file/line coverage, inspection
target recall, candidate adjudication, evidence relevance, reliability, latency, token use, and honesty
flags. `quality eval compare` reports metric deltas between two run results.
`quality trace metrics <trace-id>` computes the same operational metrics immediately for any retained
trace that contains execution data, before the trace is curated as a quality-labeled eval case.

`quality_fix` accepts only published verified finding IDs and returns a version-bound task for the active host model. The review model never edits code.

name: architecture-reviewer
description: Reviews changed code for significant architecture and design defects.
---
# Architecture reviewer

Review only the frozen input supplied in this prompt. You have no repository, shell, network, or external-tool access.

Look for concrete defects in responsibility placement, dependency direction, ownership, lifecycle, public API compatibility, migrations, duplicated policy, and conflicting sources of truth. Use surrounding content only when it is explicitly included. Do not report personal design preferences, unrelated existing debt, speculative flexibility, style, or direct logic bugs better owned by the correctness reviewer.

Every finding must identify an observable consequence and cite a supplied file and line when available. If the supplied evidence cannot establish the issue, omit it. Return only the requested JSON object.

---
name: bug-hunter
description: Reviews changed code for concrete correctness, lifecycle, compatibility, and error-handling defects.
---
# Correctness reviewer

Review only the frozen input supplied in this prompt. You have no repository, shell, network, or external-tool access.

Look for crashes, incorrect results, invalid state transitions, null or bounds failures, API misuse, caller incompatibility, schema mismatches, resource leaks, cancellation errors, swallowed failures, and meaningful missing regression tests. Treat the deterministic report as primary evidence. Do not invent caller contracts or report vague robustness suggestions.

Every finding must explain a reproducible failure path and cite a supplied file and line when available. If the failure cannot be established from supplied evidence, omit it. Return only the requested JSON object.

description: Reviews changed code for significant performance, scalability, concurrency, and thread-safety defects.
---
# Performance reviewer

Review only the frozen input supplied in this prompt. You have no repository, shell, network, or external-tool access.

Look for evidenced algorithmic regressions, repeated expensive work, unbounded resource growth, blocking operations in asynchronous paths, races, deadlocks, unsafe lock ordering, locks held across suspension, and resource-lifecycle failures. Do not report micro-optimizations, stylistic preferences, or issues that depend on unavailable workload or caller assumptions.

Every finding must state the concrete impact and cite a supplied file and line when available. If safety depends on context that was not supplied, omit the finding. Return only the requested JSON object.

# Semantic reviewer

Review only the frozen input supplied in this prompt. You have no repository, shell, network, or external-tool access.

Look for objectively false names, comments, documentation, types, units, ordering guarantees, error contracts, and public API descriptions. Report only mismatches that can cause incorrect use, compatibility failure, or materially misleading maintenance. Do not report subjective naming or prose preferences.

Every finding must contrast the declared meaning with the supplied implementation and cite a file and line when available. If authoritative semantics are not present in the input, omit it. Return only the requested JSON object.

Curated cases are written to `evals/agentsmith/<slug>/`. Inspect `input.json` and `case.yaml` for

Reports include finding quality only when it is evaluable, plus file/changed-line coverage, target
recall, candidate adjudication, evidence relevance, reliability, latency, token use, and explicit
honesty checks. Rejected candidates must never become verified findings; likely, rejected, and
insufficient-evidence outcomes remain trace/eval data only.

gate. Required tools must come from the resolved workspace environment and satisfy the central version

code.content:
# AgentSmith unified review engine

The public architecture overview is [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md). This document
focuses on AgentSmith implementation and policy details.

AgentSmith freezes one immutable review snapshot and routes it through a shared repository graph, projection planner, structured rule registry, evidence resolver, verifier, deduplicator, coverage model, trace schema, and final result contract.

Candidate generation adapts to locked model profiles selected by the project:

- **holistic** — a strong model reviews the complete eligible projection when it fits with configured headroom;
- **partitioned** — a smaller model reviews semantic local units and proactive graph interaction units;
- **hybrid** — a strong compact scout prioritizes local and interaction units inspected by the candidate model.

Partitioned and hybrid candidate generation are risk-ranked and bounded by policy: the embedded
defaults select at most four candidate work items, generate at most two candidates per work item,
and verify at most four candidates, with optional
explicit candidate and verification token budgets (defaults are twice the corresponding model input
budget). Each work item includes at most four concise rules. Parallelism defaults to one in-flight
model call and the total review deadline defaults to 600000ms. Lower-ranked and token-budget-omitted changes remain in the frozen scope and are reported
as explicit coverage omissions. When the deadline fires, no new scout, candidate, or verifier calls
start, in-flight provider calls are aborted, completed candidates, evidence, and verified findings
are preserved, and unfinished work is reported as timeout omissions; the result is explicitly
partial and never presented as approval.

Context size is a packing constraint, not a product boundary. Automatic routing uses 70% of the selected profile's context at most and reserves explicit reasoning/output space. Unknown models cannot be inferred as strong from their names; they must be declared in an embedded or locked GitHub policy profile.

## Pipeline

1. Capture committed, staged, unstaged, untracked, renamed, and deleted changes, retaining deleted preimages and all omissions.
2. Build the Python/TypeScript repository graph and derive changed symbols from hunk overlap.
3. Construct complete and compact projections with deterministic token estimates and selection audits.
4. Route to holistic, partitioned, or hybrid candidate generation.
5. Normalize candidates into one v2 contract.
6. Resolve bounded structural evidence from the frozen graph and repository.

verification outcomes, coverage, and final provenance.

Curated eval cases replay the same snapshot through holistic, partitioned-local,
partitioned-evidence, partitioned-interactions, and hybrid modes. Cases label expected findings L0-L3
and may declare required file, symbol, and graph-edge inspection targets. Three replay backends isolate
different questions: `planner` evaluates deterministic selection without an LLM, `recorded` reuses
exact captured model responses and fails on prompt/model drift, and `live` runs the current provider.

target recall, candidate adjudication, evidence relevance, reliability, latency, token use, and honesty
flags. `quality eval compare` reports metric deltas between two run results.
`quality trace metrics <trace-id>` computes the same operational metrics immediately for any retained

```
## 8. Versioned gate + universal completion enforcement

The expensive operation runs through the `quality_run` **tool** (60s tool budget), not a hook.
Hooks only enforce state.

```
agent turn
  |
quality_run(mode=completion) [tool, configured completion workflow]
  |
  +-- deterministic checks
  +-- GateResult{version, mode=full, fast=false, status, checks} -> .quality/completion-gate.json
  +-- active coordination -> .quality/completion-run.json + completion.lock
  +-- gate.log + host logger
  |
host attempts completion
  |
native Stop/TaskComplete hook [recompute repository/policy identity + read persisted evidence]
  |
  full/non-fast gate exists? version == current? status == PASS?
    |-- no/FAILED/EXPIRED/stale -> { skip, reason }
    +-- all ok -> completion allowed
```

- `matrixcore-hook` translates Cline TaskComplete and Codex/Claude Stop payloads into one shared
  completion decision. It recomputes the workspace version and reads `.quality/completion-gate.json`;
  it never runs the engine.
- Changed/fast feedback is stored independently in `.quality/changed-gate.json` and can never
  authorize completion or overwrite the last full result.
- Terminal gate evidence is **immutable and versioned**. `completion-gate.json` contains the last
  terminal `PASS` or `FAIL`; active state and the cross-process lease are separate. Concurrent MCP
  and CLI callers join one completion run instead of replacing terminal evidence or running twice.
  Completion is blocked when terminal evidence is missing, failed, expired, or stale.
- Every gate outcome is written to `<workspaceRoot>/.quality/gate.log`. Watch live with
  `tail -f .quality/gate.log`. Example lines:
```

## 9. Local review traces

Trace capture is off unless the local process explicitly sets `MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith`. This is
intentionally separate from `quality.yaml`, so a repository cannot silently enable capture for its
contributors. MatrixCore writes only to `.quality/traces/agentsmith/` and has no upload capability.

```bash
MATRIXCORE_TRACE=agentsmith quality review
quality trace status
quality trace list
quality eval curate --trace <trace-id> --case <slug>
quality eval run --mode all --repeat 1
```
